To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — So this happened. Fernhollow Photo is real!!

Hi everyone! Big work update, and I wanted to put it here before Thanksgiving because I would like to tell you this myself instead of accidentally announcing it while asking somebody to pass the stuffing.

I'm going out on my own. Fernhollow Photo LLC is officially a real business. My business. Where I am the photographer and also apparently the person who has to figure out why the website is doing that.

IT'S REAL!!

Some of you know Rosebud Lane closed at the end of October. Marisol told me on October 6, and after four years shooting for her, it was a lot to take in. I've spent so many weekends saying I work for Rosebud Lane that I still have to stop myself halfway through the sentence. That was a really big chapter for me, and I'm sad it's over even while I'm excited about what comes next. Both things, apparently. Very convenient of my brain.

Before I get into my news, I need to say how much I owe Marisol. She basically taught me everything. Not just how to make pretty pictures, but how to keep doing my job when the schedule has gone completely sideways and everyone is looking at the photographer like she might also know where the missing boutonniere went. Four years with her made me a much better photographer and a person who can remain reasonably useful in a room full of stressed-out people holding flowers.

She trusted me with her couples, gave me room to learn, and kept telling me I was ready for more. She's also referred six of her 2027 couples to me, which is a huge vote of confidence and something I don't take lightly. Marisol, if you read this, thank you. I know I've said it already. You're getting it again.

The part I want everybody to know is that this isn't an idea I had three weeks ago because I panicked. I've been planning this in my head for two years. Apparently I can spend two years thinking about a business and still be shocked when I actually start it.

I filed the LLC on October 22, on my lunch break, sitting in my car outside a Fred Meyer. Extremely glamorous business origin story. I finished the paperwork and cried a little. Then I was still in a parking lot and it was still my lunch break, so that was that.

The website went live November 1. Seeing my own name on all the official stuff was weird enough, but seeing Fernhollow Photo on an actual website where people could actually inquire about hiring me? I kept opening it again to check. As if it might have changed its mind.

And here's the part that makes me feel like I can breathe: I already have 14 weddings booked for 2027. FOURTEEN. Six came through Marisol's referrals, and eight found me on my own. June is going to be a lot, with four weddings, so if you see me that month and I seem to be mentally checking a camera battery, I probably am. There's also a wedding at Wallowa Lake in September, which I'm very excited about.

The first booking that felt completely mine was Dahlia and Ken. June 12 at Timberline. They found me through the pictures I took of a couple at Multnomah Falls and decided they wanted me to photograph their wedding. They saw my work, liked it, and picked me. I know that's how hiring a photographer works, but it feels very different when you're the photographer getting the email.

I have spent four years working hard at this. Still, there's something about a couple saying yes to you, under your own business name, that makes you want to read the email about eight times. For accuracy. I'm a professional.

Also, Dad: YES, I HAVE HEALTH INSURANCE SORTED.

I picked a marketplace plan. It starts January 1. I love you and I know why you ask, so I am putting this in writing before we're all seated around Ruthie's table and you have an audience and a dinner roll. You are allowed to be excited first. The insurance part has been handled.

And I'm not trying to do every single thing alone. Jae will second shoot the big weddings with me, paid per wedding. Having my own business does not mean I've suddenly grown extra arms, although that would make carrying equipment a lot easier. I've got bookings on the calendar, deposits coming in, and help lined up for the weddings that need two photographers. There's a plan underneath all the exclamation points.

Am I scared? Yes. Obviously. It's my name on the paperwork and my inbox and my calendar, and some days that feels great and some days I have to go look at the 14 bookings again. But I'm excited more than I'm scared. I really want to do this, and I've wanted it for a long time. I don't need everybody to pretend starting a business is nothing. I just want you to know I'm not jumping into this without looking.

Now the name, because Grandma, this part is for you.

Fernhollow is from the fern hollow trail behind your old place in Gresham. That's where I took my first real pictures with your Pentax. I don't think I knew then that photography was going to become my whole job. I just wanted to take pictures, and you let me use the camera.

When I was trying to name the business, I kept coming back to that place. It felt right to use something from the beginning, before weddings and timelines and spare batteries and me having opinions about where people should stand. So yes, Grandma, the name is for you. I wanted you to know that. Your camera started something pretty big.

Sam made me a cake to celebrate. It said FERNHOLOW.

One L short, but otherwise a very strong showing. We ate it anyway. I am happy to report the spelling did not affect the cake.

Mom, yes, Sam is coming to Thanksgiving. We're bringing rolls and the cranberry thing. And if anybody wants free family pictures while we're all together, I'll bring the camera! We can try to do them before dinner so nobody has to choose between a group photo and hot mashed potatoes. Bree, no pressure whatsoever, but if you want a few with Juniper, I'm available.

Uncle Greg, I cannot guarantee an outdoor photograph will be warm. I feel like we should establish that now.

Anyway. That's my news. I'm a business owner, which still sounds like something I'm saying as a joke, except there is paperwork and everything.

I wanted you all to hear it from me, with enough time to get the initial yelling out of the way before Thanksgiving. I'm really proud of this. Nervous, yes, but proud, and so excited to see what I can make of it.

Love you guys. Grandma, thank you for the camera. Dad, January 1. Everybody else, please practice opening your eyes at the same time for the family picture.
